entities.summary: Carlos Aguiar Retes is a Mexican cardinal of the Catholic Church who serves as the Archbishop of Mexico City. He has served as an officer of the Mexican Episcopal Conference and the Latin American Episcopal Conference (CELAM) and been president of both. He helped draft the landmark mission statement CELAM issued at the close of its 2007 conference in Aparecida. He was archbishop of Tlalnepantla from 2009 to 2017 and Bishop of Texcoco from 1997 to 2009. David Agren of the Catholic News Service calls him a "longtime ally" of Pope Francis who combines "intellectual finesse with a pastoral passion".

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As president of CELAM in 2007 and again in 2013, Cardinal Carlos Aguiar Retes played a key role in shaping the Latin American Catholic Church's response to social justice issues, including poverty reduction and human rights. His efforts helped inform Pope Francis's encyclical on climate change.
